title: The Vietnam War (1955–1975)
key_facts: Conflict between North Vietnam (and Viet Cong) and South Vietnam, heavily involving the United States and allies
Part of the wider Cold War; major escalation after the Gulf of Tonkin incident (1964)
Ended with the fall of Saigon (1975) and reunification under a communist government
causes: Decolonization and unresolved conflicts after the First Indochina War
Ideological struggle between communism and anti‑communism within the Cold War
Domestic political instability in South Vietnam
outcome: US withdrawal (Paris Peace Accords 1973) and North Vietnamese victory (1975)
Human and economic costs with lasting regional and US social impacts
Realignment of US foreign/military policy (War Powers, détente debates)

figures.name: Richard Nixon
figures.role: US President; Vietnamization and Paris Peace Accords

impacts: Shaped US domestic politics, protest movements, and media’s role in war
Influenced Cold War strategy and limits of military intervention
Long‑term effects on Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos
